report:
Reviewed the complete narrow_detail claim and all seven implementation entries plus the sole associated test after fresh capture. Requirements are separate field/associated enumeration query boundaries from owner signatures; item-specific signature demand; and enumeration without eager sibling signature/body checking. Ordinary evidence: LocalStructSym::fields is a separate tracked query from sig and consumes the existing owner binder through iter_symbols; StructSig does not contain fields. The claim does not promise an individual-field query: fields resolves the field list as one separate semantic product. LocalTraitSym::items and LocalImplSym::items are distinct tracked queries which reuse their respective sig binder, then call lower_items. Both associated.rs entries are accounted for: lower_items allocates only TraitItemDef identities and generic references, while local_associated_items dispatches to separate tracked trait/impl membership queries without requesting even the owner signature. Their complete helper chain (compute_local_associated_items, keyed_source_item, item_kind_and_name, lower_item, trait_item_def) is captured in the associated source. Empty enumeration is empty; function/type/const entries and duplicate kind/name occurrences are distinguished; constructing symbols copies syntax but does not semantically check sibling signatures or bodies. This syntactic copying is not a semantic signature/body request. LocalFnSym::sig is separately keyed by the selected function symbol, reads its CST and open_owner, and computes only its receiver/parameters/return/predicates. open_owner reuses the trait or impl header signature, not an associated-item signature list. This necessary owner environment dependency does not conflate selected-item checking with checking sibling signatures. Body checking is a separate query and is not called by enumeration or sig.

The ty::todo implementation entry explicitly records the remaining associated-type and associated-constant checked-signature APIs. Captured local type_aliases.rs and consts.rs support that deferral: these symbols carry owners and CST but only expose attrs, not checked signature queries. Existing local_impl_associated_type_value is a demand-driven normalization value operation, not the missing general type/const signature API. The prerequisite is implementing per-item signature products which reuse the owner binder and avoid eager siblings/bodies; neither ordinary function evidence nor identity-only enumeration is claimed to implement that missing part. This is an honest partial implementation, with the absent APIs visible as TODO.

The complete test set consists only of sage_meta::todo::checking_signature_narrow_detail. Its empty body has no assertions. Its comment explicitly defers query-trace checks rejecting unselected siblings/bodies and edit checks for owner binder/detail reuse. Accept this as a visible verification deferral, not evidence that the claim has been tested. Completion requires adding those trace/edit scenarios and assertions, with associated type/const cases dependent on the missing signature APIs identified above. A regression that eagerly requested sibling signatures or merged fields into owner signature could evade the present empty test; no passing-test adequacy claim is made. There are no N/A entries.

Actions actually executed: cargo fmt succeeded; cargo build succeeded with warnings; cargo test -p sage-meta --test semantic_spec checking_signature_narrow_detail passed its one TODO placeholder, which supplies no behavioral validation. Review start/read captured fresh source after comment-only evidence additions. No runtime implementation behavior changed and no behavioral regression was suspected or reproduced. Per meta.reviews.decisions, existing supported source boundaries and explicit implementation/testing deferrals account for the complete claim without further requested edits; TODO statuses remain deferred. Coordinator will run centralized delegated quality/sanity checks on the comment edits.
